step_1_create_scoped_minio_identity.note: MinIO IAM is currently EMPTY - /data/.minio.sys/config/iam/ contains only format.json (verified by ls). There are no users, no service accounts and no policies; every S3 consumer in the estate authenticates as root. So this is a new capability, not an edit.
step_1_create_scoped_minio_identity.prefer_named_user_over_svcacct: A named IAM user survives independently of the root credential and is separately revocable. A root-derived service account is conceptually a delegation of root and muddies the audit story. Use `mc admin user add`.
step_1_create_scoped_minio_identity.run_how: one-shot Job in storage ns, reusing the existing pattern at hack/disaster-recovery/00-prereqs.sh:39-40 (image minio/mc:RELEASE.2024-09-09T07-53-10Z). Server is quay.io/minio/minio RELEASE.2024-09-09T16-59-28Z, long past the introduction of admin user/policy APIs.
step_1_create_scoped_minio_identity.why_delete_is_in_the_policy: spec.backup.retentionPolicy is '14d'. barman-cloud enforces retention by deleting expired objects, so s3:DeleteObject on forge-backups/* is required or every backup after day 14 logs a retention failure. Delete is scoped to the one bucket, which is the whole point.

step_2_new_1password_item.create: a NEW 1Password item `minio-forge-pg` with fields ACCESS_KEY and SECRET_KEY. Do NOT add these as fields on the existing `minio` item.
step_2_new_1password_item.why_separate_item: components/volsync/secrets.yaml and forgejo/app/volsync.yaml use `dataFrom: extract: {key: minio}`, which makes the ENTIRE minio item - including MINIO_ROOT_*, VOLSYNC_REPO_PASSWORD and AZURE_STORAGE_KEY - available to the template context in whatever namespace mounts it. Keeping the forge credential in its own item stops devtools from ever needing a reference to the item that holds root.

step_3_amend_secrets_yaml.also: delete the comment at lines 2-5, which currently advertises 'Reuses the existing 1Password minio item - no new 1P fields needed' as a virtue. Replace it with why the credential is scoped, so the next engineer does not 'simplify' it back.

ruling_on_backup_encryption_question_3.agree: gzip-unencrypted barman should not block P2. Heph's technical analysis is right: CNPG's barmanObjectStore exposes only server-side `encryption: AES256` (SSE-S3), the minio HelmRelease sets no MINIO_KMS_* env (verified in storage/minio/app/helmrelease.yaml env block), so SSE-S3 would fail. There is no client-side option in in-tree barman. Blocking P2 on it would block on something P2 cannot fix.
ruling_on_backup_encryption_question_3.correction_to_the_reasoning: Themis grounds the argument on 'the data stays on-prem'. On-prem is not the same as protected here. inc-2026-09-15-002 (sev2, still `investigated`) records that the NFS export /volume1/minio on VDHNAS01 is exported to `*` with no host restriction, reachable from CLIENT-VLAN, SERVER-VLAN and both WireGuard remote-user networks. The bucket that backs forge-backups is on that same export. So forge-pg's unencrypted backups are readable by any LAN or VPN host today, without any credential at all. That does not change the landing verdict - P2 does not create the condition and cannot fix it - but 'stays on-prem' should not be recorded as if it meant 'stays private'.
ruling_on_backup_encryption_question_3.pre_existing_exposure_deserves_its_own_r: YES, and Atlas is right that postgres16's is the larger one. But it is already partly covered by inc-2026-09-15-002 from the NFS angle. The gap that incident does NOT cover is the credential-sharing and detection side, so I am opening one sev3 for that rather than duplicating.
ruling_on_backup_encryption_question_3.verdict_on_themis: CONFIRMED for the landing decision, with one correction to the reasoning.

answers_to_atlas.sse_test_delegated_to_mack: Conditionally acceptable, not as stated. The test-evidence rule demands an artefact, and is silent on who generates it - but it is NOT silent on who inspects it. Accepting 'Mack ran it and it worked' is the same failure mode as accepting 'I cross-checked the API value'. Conditions: (a) Mack returns the RAW artefact - a timestamped curl/SSE transcript showing wall-clock start and end, elapsed > 60s, the terminal SSE event, and a clean stream close - not a summary; (b) Atlas inspects the timestamps himself and records the measured elapsed seconds in the validated event; (c) Atlas does NOT outsource the whole thing. The gateway-level proof is yours: you can verify the stream survives past 15s through the gateway without needing a real generation. Mack's job is the real-generation 2-6 minute case, not the existence proof. Split it that way.
answers_to_atlas.timeout_premise: The change is justified, and you should stop trying to prove 15s. Three points. (1) Your evidence did not disconfirm anything: 'downstream_rq_timeout: 0' is the HCM request_timeout - the accept-to-request-headers-complete knob, default disabled - which is a DIFFERENT field from the per-route RouteAction.timeout whose documented Envoy default is 15s. You were reading the wrong field and were right to refuse to conclude from it. (2) Your websocket observation is not counter-evidence either: Envoy exempts upgraded connections from the route timeout entirely, which is exactly why the keuken kiosk survives all day on routes with no timeout set. So 'websockets work' tells you nothing about the SSE case. Your P100 of 16,000 ms is, if anything, weakly consistent with a request terminated at the 15s default. (3) In-estate corroboration you already have: someone previously hit a default request timeout truncating long-lived responses on this estate and fixed it by setting timeouts.request '0s' on the Plex route, with a comment linking the Plex forum thread. That is empirical evidence from your own tree that a non-zero default exists and bites long responses. Decisive point: the decision does not depend on the premise. If the premise is true, the policy is required. If it is false, a bounded 600s cap on one route costs nothing. If you omit it and the premise is true, every family generation is truncated. The asymmetry says act. Reframe post_4 from 'prove the 15s default' to 'measure that a stream runs past 15s uncut and completes' - that is the operationally load-bearing fact and it is provable.

findings.detail: The planned event says rollback is 'Delete the six resources.' Read literally as a kubectl delete, that is INCORRECT and will not hold: install.yaml sets prune: true with interval 30m, so Flux recreates all six objects within 30 minutes. Second footgun: deleting only the studio-ai/ directory while leaving './studio-ai/install.yaml' in kubernetes/main/apps/network/kustomization.yaml makes the network namespace build FAIL, which breaks reconciliation for that whole namespace - a far worse outcome than the change itself. The only correct rollback is `git revert 9e6deff` (or the cherry-picked equivalent), which reverses all 8 files atomically including the kustomization.yaml line, letting Flux prune the six objects. Restate it that way in the record.

findings.detail: The record declines the Backend CRD because it 'has zero users on this estate', then introduces BackendTrafficPolicy, which ALSO has zero users on this estate - I confirmed it is the only one in the tree. advisories.name: alt_svc_h3_leaks_through_the_clear_patch
advisories.reason: Caddy emits 'alt-svc: h3=":443"; ma=2592000' on every response (captured on all five probes). EnvoyPatchPolicy network/altsvc-clear-internal adds Alt-Svc: clear at RouteConfiguration scope with NO append_action; live envoy-external route config shows response_headers_to_add [{"header":{"key":"Alt-Svc","value":"clear"}}]. Envoy's HeaderValueOption.append_action defaults to APPEND_IF_EXISTS_OR_ADD, and alt-svc is not a predefined inline header, so a DUPLICATE header is added rather than the upstream value replaced. Browsers will see both 'h3=":443"' and 'clear'; RFC 7838 requires 'clear' to be the only alt-value. studio-ai is the first backend on envoy-internal that emits its own Alt-Svc (mealie and nas both return only 'alt-svc: clear'), so the patch has never been exercised in append mode. Expect QUIC attempts to 172.16.2.241:443/udp, where envoy-internal has only TCP listeners 10080/10443. This estate has a prior QUIC incident on record. Fix: set append_action REPLACE_IF_EXISTS_OR_ADD in altsvc-clear-policy.yaml (separate change, touches the shared gateway), or strip Alt-Svc on this route with a ResponseHeaderModifier filter (scoped to this change).

It also extends a latent DNS-rebinding primitive: a single future 'internal.bluejungle.net A 172.16.2.241' record would turn every internal name, including api., into a public name resolving to RFC1918 space.

checks_failed.name: hidden_3600s_route_idle_timeout
checks_failed.reason: timeouts.request: 600s does not only set the 600s request timeout. envoyproxy/gateway v1.3.0 internal/xds/translator/route.go:77 sets routeAction.IdleTimeout = idleTimeout(httpRoute) unconditionally on the default route branch, and idleTimeout() at lines 304-321 starts at 'timeout := time.Hour' and only raises it if the request timeout exceeds 1h. rt=600s -> 3600 !< 600 -> returns 3600s. So the rendered route will be timeout: 600s AND idle_timeout: 3600s. Model confirmed against live data on both branches: media/plex sets timeouts.request/backendRequest '0s' and renders idle_timeout '0s'; every route WITHOUT Gateway API timeouts (hass, echo-server, flux-webhook, tesla, it-tools) has idle_timeout absent, because idleTimeout() returns nil when rt==nil. Consequence: this one route lifts the idle ceiling on the SHARED family-critical listener from the HCM default of 300s to one hour, for streams that need zero backend work to hold. There is no ClientTrafficPolicy on envoy-internal (kubectl get clienttrafficpolicy -A: none), no SecurityPolicy anywhere on the estate, no NetworkPolicy, and no rate limit. Blast radius is the same 2-replica envoy pod that serves the keuken kiosk, HA, Grafana, zigbee2mqtt, zwave, evcc and pgadmin: envoy container limit memory 1Gi, no CPU limit, fixed_heap 858993459 with overload action stop_accepting_requests at 0.98, global max_active_downstream_connections 50000, downstream http2 max_concurrent_streams 100. The change record's stated idle reasoning ('connectionIdleTimeout is left at Envoy's 300s stream_idle_timeout default') was wrong by 12x, and the refactor to the native field did not change this: getEffectiveRequestTimeout (route.go:288-302) reads BOTH the native timeouts.request and BackendTrafficPolicy requestTimeout, so both forms produce idle_timeout 3600s.

sixth_finding_alt_svc.bonus_it_is_safe_under_BOTH_orderings: If most_specific_header_mutations_wins were ever flipped to true, the order becomes {global, vhost, route}: the add would append 'clear' alongside h3, then the route-level remove would strip ALL Alt-Svc headers, yielding no Alt-Svc at all. Still no h3 advertisement, so no QUIC attempt - only the 'clear' eviction directive would be lost. The fix does not depend on a default staying put.
sixth_finding_alt_svc.eg_renders_it_at_the_most_specific_level: envoyproxy/gateway v1.3.0 internal/xds/translator/route.go:48-50 'if len(httpRoute.RemoveResponseHeaders) > 0 { router.ResponseHeadersToRemove = httpRoute.RemoveResponseHeaders }' on the *routev3.Route - i.e. route-entry scope. internal/gatewayapi/filters.go:735-767 only rejects empty header names and de-dupes; 'Alt-Svc' is accepted and no allow/deny list applies.
sixth_finding_alt_svc.name: alt_svc_h3_leaks_through_the_clear_patch
sixth_finding_alt_svc.ordering_PROVEN: Running data plane is Envoy 1.33.0 (admin /server_info: b0f43d67.../1.33.0/Clean/RELEASE/BoringSSL). Live config_dump of RouteConfiguration 'network/envoy-internal/https': most_specific_header_mutations_wins is ABSENT (=false), response_headers_to_add=[{"header":{"key":"Alt-Svc","value":"clear"}}] with no append_action. Envoy v1.33.0 source/common/router/config_impl.cc:996-1004 finalizeResponseHeaders iterates getResponseHeaderParsers(specificity_ascend = mostSpecificHeaderMutationsWins()); config_impl.cc:179-190 getHeaderParsers returns {route_header_parser, vhost_header_parser, global_route_config_header_parser} when specificity_ascend is FALSE ('Sorted from most to least specific'). So: route-level remove runs FIRST and deletes Caddy's h3 value, THEN the RouteConfiguration-level add fires APPEND_IF_EXISTS_OR_ADD onto an absent header and produces exactly one 'Alt-Svc: clear'. Atlas's assumption is correct.
sixth_finding_alt_svc.post_landing_assertion_still_required: Assert on a real response through the gateway: exactly ONE alt-svc header AND its value exactly 'clear'. e.g. curl -sD- https://chat.bluejungle.net/ -o /dev/null | grep -ci '^alt-svc' must equal 1, and the value must not contain 'h3'. This is the empirical closure; everything above is static proof.
sixth_finding_alt_svc.premise_still_live: Re-probed 2026-09-21T13:19:40Z through SNI studio.bluejungle.net on 172.16.2.200: /v1/models no key -> HTTP/2 401 + 'alt-svc: h3=":443"; ma=2592000'; /v1/models wrong bearer -> 401 + same; /api/tags no key -> 401 + same; chat host / -> 503 x-household-mode: building + same. Exactly 1 alt-svc header from Caddy on every response. Without the filter, every response through the gateway would carry both h3 and clear.

corrections_to_the_brief_found_during_in: fixed_heap_pressure is an INTEGER PERCENT (0-100), not a 0-1 ratio. Proven: gauge reads 3 while envoy_server_memory_heap_size=31457280 and max_heap_size_bytes=858993459 -> 31457280/858993459 = 3.66% -> floor 3. An alert written as '> 0.9' as the brief's framing implies would fire IMMEDIATELY and PERMANENTLY at today's value. This is the single most important finding of the inventory.

The monitor tracks memory_HEAP_SIZE, not memory_allocated. Argus's 77x headroom was computed from memory_allocated (11.4 MB). The series actually driving the trigger is heap_size (31.4 MB), so real headroom to the 0.98 action is ~27x, not 77x. Still ample; the number in the record was wrong.

The brief says 'no memory request'. FALSE - the envoy container has requests.memory=1Gi equal to limits.memory=1Gi. It is Burstable only because CPU has a request (100m) and no limit. Memory is guaranteed and the pod is not a memory-eviction candidate. The CPU-limit half of the claim is correct.
Argus's 'baseline 1 and 1' for listener rq_active is an instantaneous read. 7d max_over_time is 8 and 4. Thresholds sized off the 7d maximum, not the spot value.

payload.obl_2_alert_decomposition_better_than_al: 'Alert on any non-401' would page on a 503, and a 503 is what the gateway returns whenever the Mac Studio - a desktop - is asleep or Caddy is mid-build. Measured: chat.bluejungle.net returns probe_http_status_code 503 right now; a genuinely unreachable target returns 0; NXDOMAIN returns 0. So the assertion is split by status class: 2xx/3xx => AiEdgeUnauthenticatedAccessPossible (CRITICAL, pages - the endpoint served an unauthenticated request); 4xx-other-than-401 => AiEdgeAuthAssertionUnexpectedStatus (warning - auth semantics changed); 5xx/0 => already covered by the pre-existing generic BlackboxProbeFailure at warning, and deliberately does NOT page because a sleeping desktop is not a security event.
payload.obl_2_probe: New blackbox module http_401_unauthenticated with valid_status_codes: [401] + fail_if_not_ssl: true. Probe CR ai-edge-auth, 2 targets: https://api.bluejungle.net/v1/models and https://api.bluejungle.net/api/tags, interval 60s.
payload.obl_2_scope_judgement: EXCLUDING /api/pull and both path-traversal variants from Mack's suggested set, with reasons: (a) /api/pull is a MUTATING endpoint - if auth is ever dropped, a probe hitting it every 60s is a monitor that could trigger model-download work on the Mac Studio. Monitoring must never mutate. (b) The traversal variants add ZERO discriminating power to an UNAUTHENTICATED assertion - measured, all five paths return an identical 401 today, and all five would flip together if auth dropped. The normalisation-parity question they were meant to answer can only be asked WITH a valid key, and putting a household LLM API key into the cluster to satisfy a monitoring probe would weaken the very posture the probe exists to protect.

payload.UNREQUESTED_FIX_THAT_WOULD_HAVE_MADE_obl: blackbox.yml is mounted with subPath. Kubernetes NEVER propagates ConfigMap updates into a subPath mount, and the blackbox-exporter Deployment carried no reloader annotation (checked: no pod annotations, no deployment annotations, pod Running 98d). So on cherry-pick the ConfigMap object would have updated while the file inside the container stayed frozen at its 98-day-old content. The exporter would have answered `Unknown module "http_401_unauthenticated"` to the new Probe, the scrape would have failed, and NO probe_success series would exist at all - meaning neither the two new alerts NOR the pre-existing generic BlackboxProbeFailure could fire. A probe that looks installed and asserts nothing. Fixed by adding reloader.stakater.com/auto: "true", matching the 20 other apps in this repo that use it. Verified stakater/reloader v1.4.14 is Running 170d in kube-system, is cluster-scoped (RELOADER_NAMESPACE empty), and demonstrably acts - its log shows it restarting tesla-http-proxy on a secret change on 2026-07-19.

dns_design.conflict_rule: The manual record and an unannotated HTTPRoute must not coexist, or external-dns-unifi would try to create forge.bluejungle.net itself. The route annotation must be live BEFORE the manual record is written.
dns_design.measured_controller_none: keuken/kantoor have controller:none -> no k8s.unifi owner TXT, no Cloudflare record (DoH NXDOMAIN), external-dns-unifi logs 'All records are already up to date' every minute with no churn. So controller:none suppresses BOTH instances.
dns_design.pattern: LAN-only (same as keuken/kantoor): HTTPRoute carries external-dns.alpha.kubernetes.io/controller: none, plus ONE manual UniFi static A record.
dns_design.why_not_default_pattern: The default envoy-internal route makes external-dns-cloudflare-internal publish forge CNAME internal.bluejungle.net to PUBLIC Cloudflare. That is a Cloudflare write outside the approved list, it advertises that a client-repo forge exists, and it does not work for DoH anyway: internal.bluejungle.net is NXDOMAIN publicly (measured via DoH), so it is a dangling CNAME.

advisories.summary: Container capabilities. open-webui (uid 0) and the hermes main container keep the runtime-default capability set, including NET_RAW, MKNOD, SYS_CHROOT and SETFCAP.

Chat retention and admin visibility. Open WebUI v0.11.3 has NO chat retention setting, so children's chats live in webui.db indefinitely. Hermes sessions prune at 30 days (Mack config sessions.retention_days: 30). Hermes memories persist by design. Backups hold about 28 days, plus up to 7 days of prune lag. Even with B2 fixed, the admin can still set a child's password (routers/users.py:963-971), and the cluster admin can read webui.db and Hermes state.db. The promise 'nobody sees your conversations' on the ladder page is policy, not a technical control.

advisories.remediation: Restrict it to the cluster.local search walk (e.g. matchPattern '**.cluster.local' on Cilium 1.19; validate) and test a mover run.
advisories.summary: The volsync-mover DNS allow-list is '*', which permits DNS exfiltration through CoreDNS -> UDM from pods that read every PVC.

hermes image pinned by digest only (no tag), so Renovate cannot track it. The image carries 19 CRITICAL / 428 HIGH, 16 of the criticals fixable upstream: perl, mbedtls, node tar CVE-2026-59873, anyio CVE-2026-63374.

advisories.remediation: Reject tar members of type l/h from 'tar -tvzf' before extracting. Use an allow-list: config.yaml, SOUL.md, plugins/**, skills/**. Also refuse .env and auth.json.
advisories.summary: seed-once.sh checks for symlinks AFTER extraction and never checks hardlinks. The state-path check is a top-level deny-list. Risk is bounded: the bundle is SOPS-encrypted and author-trusted, and the init runs as 10000 with no capabilities. The sha256 checks give integrity only, not authenticity.

advisories.remediation: Grafana auth.generic_oauth role_attribute_strict: true, or restrict the Authelia OIDC authorization policy to group admins.
advisories.summary: Creating lldap accounts for the children widens Grafana. The Authelia grafana OIDC client only requires two_factor, and Grafana role_attribute_path returns null for them, so without role_attribute_strict they fall back to Viewer. A child who enrols a 2FA device via an email they control can log in.

Authelia networks: private is not a control. Every source Authelia can see on this path is RFC1918, including cloudflared pods if the route were ever exposed. The explicit deny rule is the real fail-safe. The route also lacks /ladder and /telt-niet (Mack Q4); adding them is security-neutral.

blockers.name: gezinsdienst_header_trust_reachable_in_cluster
blockers.reason: Mack's gezinsdienst.py authorizes GET /, GET /v1/overzicht, POST /besproken/<id> and POST /telt-niet/<id> ONLY on Remote-User/Remote-Groups (lines 633-686; the Origin==Host check is client-forgeable). Its own docstring (lines 14-16) requires that 'the NetworkPolicy must make envoy the only ingress for those paths'. network-policies/app/gezinsdienst.yaml allows hermes -> 8080 at L4 with no path restriction. Any code running in a Hermes pod can send Remote-Groups: ouders directly. It can then read every child's safety signals, mark them besproken (which suppresses the doorbell repeat), or telt-niet the ladder entries.
blockers.remediation: Add Cilium L7 rules to the hermes ingress rule: toPorts 8080 rules.http [{method: POST, path: '/v1/(signaal|gedrag|gebruik)'}]. Test from a hermes pod: GET / with forged Remote-Groups gives 403 from the Cilium proxy plus a Hubble L7 DROPPED, and POST /v1/gebruik with its token gives 200.

blockers.name: admin_reads_children_messages_via_analytics
blockers.reason: ENABLE_ADMIN_CHAT_ACCESS=false does not stop the admin reading chat content. ENABLE_ADMIN_ANALYTICS defaults True (config.py:2108), so main.py:855 mounts /api/v1/analytics. GET /api/v1/analytics/messages?user_id=<child> (routers/analytics.py:125-150, get_admin_user) returns ChatMessageModel, which includes content (models/chat_messages.py:188).
blockers.remediation: Set ENABLE_ADMIN_ANALYTICS=false in open-webui/app/deployment.yaml before the first start. Test: GET /api/v1/analytics/summary as admin returns 404.

recommended_design.problem_1_fronting: Per-hostname HTTPS listeners on envoy-internal for the 5 admin hosts (https-hass-code, https-node-red, https-zigbee2mqtt, https-zwave, https-esphome; same wildcard cert), routes moved to those sectionNames. Coalescing guard: an HTTPRoute on the catch-all https listener for the 5 hostnames with HTTPRouteFilter directResponse 421 (native EG 1.3), and an EnvoyPatchPolicy adding a domains:[*] direct_response 421 vhost to each dedicated RDS (browser connection reuse otherwise gives 404). Extend altsvc-clear-internal EPP to the 5 new RDS names. Extend L5 ClientTrafficPolicy envoy-internal-strip-remote targetRefs with the 5 new sectionNames (it targets sectionName https only). Rejected: global Lua via EnvoyPatchPolicy index-path into http_filters (fragile on a family-critical gateway, NACK risk), EnvoyExtensionPolicy Lua (not implemented in 1.3), strict_sni_host_matching (does not exist in Envoy 1.33), EG upgrade (out of scope, pinned).
recommended_design.problem_2_auth: Authelia ext-authz SecurityPolicy per HTTPRoute (the L5 pattern, failOpen false), in home-automation, ReferenceGrant security/home-automation-ext-authz (SecurityPolicy from home-automation -> Service authelia only). Authelia rule ABOVE the *.domain wildcard: domains hass-code, node-red, zigbee2mqtt, zwave, esphome -> two_factor, subject group:admins (pending Q2), networks private; followed by an explicit deny for the same domains. PLUS app-native closure of the non-Envoy paths (F1/F2): remove port 12321 from the LB Service (ClusterIP-only Service home-assistant-code for the route) and code-server --auth password with HASHED_PASSWORD from 1Password (or remove the sidecar, Q1); ESPHome dashboard USERNAME/PASSWORD from 1Password (verify env support in 2026.6.2 entrypoint at build). node-red: decommission (Q3) else adminAuth in settings.js.

checks_failed.reason: The ESO template renders ESPHOME_USERNAME/PASSWORD with no guard. (a) If the 1P fields exist but are empty, both-empty means auth OFF in device-builder ('both or neither'): fail OPEN while every check says Ready. (b) If a field label is misspelt, the dataFrom extract map lacks the key and Go text/template renders '<no value>', so the dashboard is protected by the literal password '<no value>': fail WEAK. (c) If the item is missing, the Secret never exists, the upgrade times out, and the HelmRelease rolls back (upgrade.remediation.strategy rollback, retries 3) to the unauthenticated revision: fail OPEN.

checks_failed.name: rollback_to_unauthenticated_revision

checks_failed.name: open_webui_admin_one_factor
checks_failed.reason: The client authorization policy grants one_factor to group admins, and OAUTH_ADMIN_ROLES=admins makes them Open WebUI admin. An Open WebUI admin can install Functions/Tools (server-side Python) in a pod that holds every child conversation (webui.db), MODEL_API_KEY and the Hermes API keys. A family member who learns the parent lldap password (shoulder-surfing, a shared device) would get that with no second factor. This is inconsistent with D1 (ouders two_factor for the far smaller gezin page).

payload.remediation_advice: In authorization_policies.open-webui.rules put FIRST: policy two_factor, subject [group:admins]; then the existing one_factor rule for group:gezin and group:owui-keuken (drop admins from it); default deny unchanged. The admin already has 2FA enrolled (the grafana client is two_factor). Test: an admins login is asked for 2FA, and a gezin login is not. Everything else in d0a1a04 passes: PKCE S256 required, client_secret_basic, the exact redirect URI, and the bcrypt digest from ESO (32..72 alnum guard; refreshInterval 0 is fine, rotation is a manual re-sync).

passed.land-2 d8ec4c7: PASS. OIDC proxy design is sound. The nginx sidecar (non-root 101, drop ALL, read-only root FS) listens on 127.0.0.1:443 only. PKCE S256 + client_secret_basic, MERGE_ACCOUNTS_BY_EMAIL=false, OAUTH_ALLOWED_ROLES enforced, group creation off. The L7 CNP pins the whole pod (app container included) to the same four Authelia calls. e07c2a5 adopted R1/R2. The pod-private CA can mint any name but is trusted only inside this pod, so it adds no new trust boundary.

payload.hermod_udm_check: Read-only, controller 10.6.106: Sander premise does not hold. Threat Management is IDS (alert-only, blocks nothing) on CLIENT/GUEST; worker nodes 172.16.2.81-83 are on the ips_suppression whitelist (not even alerted); DNS Protection filter is none on all networks; only network-scoped ad-block applies (CLIENT-VLAN), no per-client or stricter kid filter. So the boys devices get ad-block + IDS alerts, and agent egress via nodes gets ad-block only (if the proxy resolves via the UDM). Options to Sander: accept; malware-only DoH resolver for the proxy (e.g. 1.1.1.2) scoped to the agents; or UDM-wide change (high, affects all clients).
